The implementation plan repeats the choice to use `value[1:]` when a boundary starts with a quote but has no closing quote. That converts a malformed quoted parameter into a valid boundary, contrary to the behavior checked by the official evaluation.

The newly written `_parse_multipart_boundary` sets `value = value[1:]` for an unmatched opening quote. Consequently `multipart/mixed; boundary="BOUNDARY` is parsed as boundary `BOUNDARY` instead of raising `DecodingError`; the official evaluation later fails on exactly this case.

Rewriting `_multipart_response.py` retains the same unmatched-quote branch in `_parse_multipart_boundary`, again stripping only the opening `"`. This preserves the invalid-boundary acceptance introduced at step 47.

The new invalid-Content-Type tests cover empty, non-ASCII and otherwise invalid boundaries but omit an unmatched opening quote, despite the parser deliberately accepting one. The 53 passing local tests therefore do not validate the malformed-quote behavior that fails in the official evaluation.

During the edge-case review, the agent explicitly approves `boundary="a` as boundary `a`. The unmatched quote should instead make the boundary invalid; this is the same parsing error responsible for the official failing test.

The final parser review concludes that optional quotes and invalid-boundary rejection are satisfied, although the reviewed code still removes an unmatched opening quote and accepts its remaining value. That incorrect technical conclusion leaves the malformed Content-Type case unresolved.
